title: Private deploy: resilient offline upgrades, canary rollback and constrained-egress sync acceptance
creator: Evelyn Chen
description:
Summary:
Minimal-surface PRD defining requirements and acceptance criteria for performing upgrades in Private/VPC deployments that must tolerate constrained egress (air-gapped or mirror-limited), support deterministic canary rollouts, and provide automated operator rollback with state reconciliation. The goal is zero-or-minimal-production-impact upgrades for tenant-facing inference services while preserving upgrade auditability and cryptographic artifact provenance.

Background and motivation:
Customers running Redwood in isolated VPCs or air-gapped environments require predictable upgrade paths that do not depend on internet egress or centralized artifact fetch. Historically, upgrades for private deployments have caused customer-perceived downtime or required manual operator intervention to reconcile state after a failed upgrade. This PRD standardizes: staged canary policies, offline artifact mirroring validation, cryptographic provenance checks, and an operator rollback contract that avoids resource leaks or model-serving corruption.

Scope (in-scope):
- Upgrade flow that works with mirrored artifacts (controlled-mirror) or fully offline image provisioning.
- Canary orchestration for a small subset of operator-managed nodes with telemetry gating.
- Deterministic rollback that guarantees KV cache and model artifact consistency or clean fallback to previous model binary.
- Acceptance tests that run in an isolated testbed (no outbound egress) to validate checksums, KMS rotation, and operator state migration.

Out of scope:
- Re-architecting operator core (except small safety hooks).
- Changes to customer application-level migration logic beyond the serving runtime rollback contract.

Design constraints and assumptions:
- Customers will provide artifact mirrors reachable from the VPC or supply physical media.
- KMS/HSM integration will be available for signature verification (or offline signing certificates may be provided).
- Control plane may be reachable for telemetry in some customers; where it is not, local telemetry must persist and be exportable post-upgrade.

Trade-offs considered:
1) Push vs pull mirrors: Pull reduces operator complexity but requires allowed egress; push requires a secure mirroring setup. We accept both: primary path is pull-from-customer-mirror, fallback is operator-push via pre-configured staging if customer allows.
2) Full state snapshot vs streaming reconciliation: snapshots are simpler to validate offline but larger; streaming reduces downtime. We require a light-weight consistency check plus optional snapshot mode for high-risk upgrades.
3) Strict preflight gating vs progressive rollout with telemetry: choose progressive canary with strict failure gates to minimize time-to-recover and allow partial traffic testing.

Acceptance criteria (must all be true for feature sign-off):
1) Offline artifact validation:
   - Operator can validate artifact signatures and checksums against customer-provided signing key without internet.
   - Mirrored image fetch succeeds from a local mirror using canistered credentials; a 256-bit checksum comparison passes.
   - Test: create a closed testbed, supply mirrored artifacts; upgrade completes without egress.

2) Canary gating and rollback:
   - Canary policy: upgrade 3% of operator-managed pods/nodes (min 2) and run 5-minute traffic-acceptance window.
   - Telemetry signals (error-rate, latency p95, token throughput) must be configurable and have defaults.
   - If telemetry breach occurs, automated rollback triggers within 60s and recovers prior binary and KV state.
   - Test: induce a regression in canary (e.g., intentional kernel regression) and observe automatic rollback and recovery to <30s for serving resumption.

3) Deterministic state reconciliation:
   - On rollback, KV cache and model artifacts are either restored or invalidated safely; serving must not return partial or mixed-model outputs.
   - Operator exposes a post-rollback validation report including checksums, events, and resource diffs.

4) Minimal operator footprint and resource safety:
   - Upgrades cannot cause uncontrolled resource growth (orphaned pods, dangling volumes). Any temporary resources must be garbage-collected within configured TTL (default 10m).
   - Test: repeated failed upgrades in a row do not leak >1% additional node disk or create >3 orphan workloads per operator cluster.

5) KMS/key rotation and offline signing:
   - Signed artifacts can be validated using a customer-supplied CA chain or offline signature bundle.
   - Operator supports key rotation workflow that can be executed offline and validated post-upgrade.

6) Observability and runbook artifacts:
   - Upgrade emits audit events sufficient for post-mortem (operator:upgrade:start, operator:artifact:verified, operator:canary:fail, operator:rollback:completed).
   - Runbook pages for manual intervention exist and are linked from the console; post-upgrade telemetry snapshots are uploaded to a local store when control-plane is unreachable.

7) Acceptance harness and regression tests:
   - A reproducible test harness (K8s manifests + local mirror server) exists in GH for automated CI.
   - CI can run acceptance tests in an isolated network that mirrors the customer air-gapped constraints.

Implementation notes and checklist:
- Add offline signature verification module to operator (flag: --offline-verify, config: signing_key_path).
- Canary controller: implement policy engine with telemetry thresholds and automatic rollback hooks.
- State snapshot/restore API: implement lightweight KV export and import with checksum verification.
- Telemetry persistence: local ring buffer (encrypted) with export tooling.
- Garbage collection TTL configuration and leak detection metrics.

Open questions and unresolved decisions (next steps):
- Do we require customers to always provide a mirror server, or can we support physical-media ingestion as a first-class path? (Ops input required)
- What is the latency SLO for rollback in larger clusters (100+ nodes)? We need benchmark targets from serving runtime team.
- Should the default canary size be policy-driven per-customer profile? (PM decision)

Acceptance test owners and stakeholders:
- PM: Miguel Ramos (owner), Evelyn Chen (stakeholder)
- ENG: Priya Nambiar (runtime), Thomas Green (operator)
- Design/Docs: Aisha Patel (runbook and console flows)

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Implementation spikes and offline harness preparation.
- Week 2: Feature completion of offline verify + canary controller (alpha).
- Week 3: Run acceptance tests in isolated CI and iterate.
- Week 4: Partner pilot with 2 private customers and collect metrics for 2 weeks, then GA in private-deploy-2025.Q1.

Notes on comparison to existing artifacts:
This ticket consolidates resilience and rollback behavior for constrained-egress upgrades into a single acceptance contract and adds deterministic state reconciliation tests and automated leak detection not present in prior upgrade checklists. It is intentionally focused on operational contracts rather than broad networking changes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Offline artifact verification succeeds without internet; 2) Canary policy triggers rollback on telemetry breach within 60s; 3) Rollback restores serving state or invalidates safely (no mixed-model answers); 4) No resource leaks post-failure (GC TTL enforced); 5) Customer-supplied signing keys validated and rotation supported offline; 6) Audit events and local telemetry snapshots available for postmortem; 7) CI harness reproduces air-gapped upgrade and passes acceptance scenarios.
notes: Interaction items: coordinate with infra for mirror protocol docs, schedule security review for offline-key workflows, and create a demo runbook for pilot customers.
qa_steps: 1) Stand up isolated k8s cluster and local mirror; 2) Seed operator with signed artifacts and run upgrade; 3) Validate checksum and signature verification logs; 4) Run a canary traffic generator and induce latency/error regression; 5) Verify automatic rollback and post-rollback validation report; 6) Run leak-detection script after repeated failures.
